chunks: From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, [from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak], from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) or he said, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).
He said: There is no one except that there is a vein of leprosy in him, so melt it by eating the turnip.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of eating turnips according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam (peace be upon him) identifies a universal physiological or spiritual predisposition to leprosy (or impurity) in every human, prescribing the consumption of turnips (*saljam*) as a therapeutic means to 'melt' or alleviate this condition. This reflects the Shia tradition of linking physical health with spiritual purity, where dietary remedies are seen as both medicinal and purificatory, aligning with the broader Islamic emphasis on maintaining the body as a trust from God.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Al Mubarak, from Abduall Bin Jabala, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, or said, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘There is no one except with him is a vein of the leprosy, therefore melt it by eating the turnip’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak [from ‘Abd Allah ibn al- Mubarak] from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan or abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
Everyone has a vein of leprosy so you should dissolve it with turnips.’”
